Configure Multi-Tree (multiPhylo) Sampling and Ensemble Options

Source: R/structure_phylo.R
tree_control.Rd

Attaches multi-tree sampling specifications to a multiPhylo object. By default in because.phybase (>= 1.1.0), multiPhylo objects use "ensemble" mode (Bayesian Model Averaging across trees with deterministic chain-to-tree assignment, defaulting to n.chains = 2 chains per tree so within-tree convergence can be separated from between-tree phylogenetic sensitivity). Users can optionally select method = "dcat" to use the categorical index variable (K_tree ~ dcat(p[])).

Usage

tree_control(
  tree,
  method = c("ensemble", "dcat"),
  n.chains = 2L,
  backbone = NULL
)

Arguments

tree

A multiPhylo object from the ape package, or a named list of multiPhylo / phylo objects representing multiple phylogenetic backbones (e.g., list(Jetz = jetz_trees, McTavish = mctav_trees)).

method

Character string specifying the multi-tree sampling strategy:

  • "ensemble" (default): Runs replicate MCMC chains assigned deterministically to individual trees to produce an exact Bayesian Model Average (BMA).

  • "dcat": Samples a discrete tree index dynamically via Gibbs sampling.

n.chains

Integer. Number of MCMC chains to run per tree in "ensemble" mode (default 2).

backbone

Optional character vector specifying the backbone name for each tree. Automatically inferred if tree is a named list.

Value

The multiPhylo object with "tree_method" and "n.chains" attributes attached.

The multiPhylo object with "tree_method", "n.chains", and optional "backbone" attributes attached.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Default ensemble mode with 2 chains per tree
trees <- tree_control(my_multiphylo, method = "ensemble", n.chains = 2)

# Legacy categorical tree-index mode
trees_dcat <- tree_control(my_multiphylo, method = "dcat")
} # }
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Standard ensemble mode
trees <- tree_control(my_multiphylo, method = "ensemble", n.chains = 2)

# Multi-backbone ensemble mode
trees_bb <- tree_control(list(Jetz = jetz_trees, McTavish = mctav_trees), n.chains = 2)
} # }
